description: A `mutual_hello` payload whose `identity` descriptor carries an unrecognized key INSIDE `extensions`. RFC-AITP-0001 §7: unknown keys inside the extension namespace MUST be ignored, never rejected — forward compatibility rides exclusively on the namespace. The identity descriptor reserves an `extensions` slot like every other signed object; it is not an exception to that rule. Receivers MUST verify the identity normally and succeed. Counterpart: id-008, which carries a forbidden member OUTSIDE the namespace and MUST fail.

expected.rationale: `vendor.example/attestation_tier` sits inside `identity.extensions`, so RFC-AITP-0001 §7's MUST-ignore applies. A verifier that rejects it is over-enforcing §7 — the asymmetry between an unknown member beside the namespace (reject) and an unknown key inside it (ignore) is deliberate.

$comment: Accept-side counterpart to id-008, and the fixture that pins the identity descriptor's `extensions` slot as real (issue #40). The handshake schema's mirror of the descriptor had no `extensions` property at all while the canonical schema did, so a descriptor carrying `extensions` validated standalone and failed inside a handshake payload — an implementation could enforce RFC-AITP-0001 §7 by rejecting every unrecognized member and pass every reject fixture while violating §7's MUST-ignore half for this artifact. That half is only observable here.
